Requirement 1

GIVE QUALITY FEEDBACK

Quality feedback goes beyond praise or personal opinion. It gives the designer precise evidence and a realistic next step they can act on.

What makes quality feedback?

Useful feedback helps the designer understand exactly what works, what needs attention and what they can realistically do next. It comments on the work and its effect on the audience, not the person who made it.

1SPECIFIC

Name the exact page, message, image, button or moment you are commenting on.

2CONSTRUCTIVE

Be respectful and balanced. Explain a strength as well as something that can improve.

3ACTIONABLE

Suggest a clear, realistic change the designer can make within the time available.

4EVIDENCE-BASED

Explain what happened during testing and how it affected understanding, trust or action.

Specific+Constructive+Actionable+Evidence-based

Useful feedback or too vague?

Classify all four examples. Useful feedback identifies a specific event and a realistic next action.

0 of 4 correct
“It looks good.”
“On my phone, the Donate button appeared after a long block of text, so I nearly missed it. Move it higher and increase the contrast.”
“I don't like green.”
“When I tried to return home, the logo did not work as a link. Make it clickable and test the route again.”
Requirement 2

PREPARE THE TEST

Choose two peers, give them neutral tasks and record the main device used. A task tells them what to achieve, not how to achieve it.

Testing setup

Do not coach the testers. If they ask where something is, reply: “What would you try next?” Their difficulty is useful evidence.

Four neutral test tasks

Tick each task only after your tester has attempted it.

Requirement 3

COLLECT PEER FEEDBACK

Ask two peers to type their feedback directly into the workbook. Each person gives two clear strengths and two practical improvements.

BE SPECIFIC AND HELPFUL

WWW identifies exactly what works and why. EBI names one realistic change that would make the campaign clearer, easier to use or more persuasive. Avoid comments such as “It is good” or “Add more colour”.

Requirement 7

JUDGE THE EVIDENCE

Choose the statement that best matches the evidence in your final campaign. Be honest and use the lowest level that accurately describes the whole strand.

Best-fit assessment

Secure is the expected standard. Mastery requires a consistently polished campaign, not one excellent feature. Your overall tier updates as you select evidence statements.

Brand identityLogo and house style
MessagePersuasion and accuracy
Social advertImpact and platform
WebsitePurpose and usability
CampaignCoherence and refinement

Complete all five strands

Your best-fit tier will appear here. Mastery requires at least four Mastery strands and no Developing strand. Secure requires at least four strands at Secure or above.

Key terms

Testing and assessment vocabularyUse these terms when you discuss feedback, improvements and the quality of the final campaign.
12 terms
Peer testingWatching another person attempt realistic tasks with your product.
Target userA person who represents the campaign's intended audience.
Neutral taskA goal that does not reveal where to click or what answer to give.
ObservationWhat the tester actually did, said or struggled to find.
EvidenceA specific event that supports a judgement or improvement.
ImpactHow an issue affects understanding, trust, access or action.
DIRTDedicated Improvement and Reflection Time used to make purposeful changes.
UsabilityHow easily a user can understand and operate a product.
AccessibilityDesigning content so more people can perceive, understand and use it.
Call to actionA clear instruction that tells the audience what to do next.
House styleThe consistent colours, type, imagery and layout used across a campaign.
Best fitThe level that most accurately describes the whole body of evidence.

Campaign assessment criteria

Developing identifies what still needs work. Secure is the expected standard. Mastery is consistently polished, purposeful and independently refined.
